description.p: Queue, pause, resume and monitor file and torrent downloads with smart auto-resume, segmented transfers, and per-file torrent picking, all in a native GNOME interface.
Filter and search the queue, retry failures in bulk, and keep everything organized with a download history that survives restarts.
Paste a video link to fetch it in up to 4K quality or as audio-only, with the title and quality picked before you add it to the queue.

ul.li: The application ID is now io.github.linuxuser67.Grab; settings from earlier versions start fresh under the new ID.
Dropped two Flatpak permissions rejected by the Flathub linter.
Refreshed the app screenshots.
Check for Updates in Preferences now checks yt-dlp, ffmpeg, and quickjs together, with a single Update button.
On new installs, keeping original file dates is now on by default, and scheduled downloads are off by default.
Validation errors on the URL and torrent fields are now exposed to assistive technologies.
Invalid URL errors are now shown on the URL field itself, and torrent file errors on the torrent row, instead of in a caption under the URL bar.
The URL bar is now a proper text entry with the action buttons beside it.
Playlist and torrent picker pills are capped at four per row, and overlong titles are truncated so one long title no longer stretches every pill.
Fixed a crash when decoding filenames with invalid percent-encoded characters.
The lookup spinner now swaps in place of the Add button, so starting a lookup no longer shifts the layout.
The URL bar is now a proper text entry with the action buttons beside it.
Playlist and torrent picker pills are capped at four per row, and overlong titles are truncated so one long title no longer stretches every pill.
Fixed a crash when decoding filenames with invalid percent-encoded characters.
The lookup spinner now swaps in place of the Add button, so starting a lookup no longer shifts the layout.
Fixed Adwaita warnings: the schedule date/time rows now live in a preferences group.
Schedule downloads for a later time: pick a date and time when adding, or let overdue items start on launch.
Download rows now show file-type icons, and the status filter is a segmented control.
Playlist and torrent pickers no longer leave empty space below short lists.
Schedule downloads for a later time: pick a date and time when adding, or let overdue items start on launch.
Download rows now show file-type icons, and the status filter is a segmented control.
Suspend inhibition now works in the Flatpak: the D-Bus parameters are built explicitly.
Filenames, paths, URLs, and error messages containing &, <, or > no longer break toast and dialog labels.
Restored finished video downloads keep their video icon after restart.
The Add button becomes a labeled pill once a playlist finishes resolving.
Playlist and torrent picker entries are now toggle pills with 12px HIG padding; the grid wraps automatically with no horizontal scrolling.
The Add button becomes a labeled pill once a media format is picked.
Overlong picker titles ellipsize instead of breaking layout measurements.
Playlist and torrent picker entries are now toggle pills with 12px HIG padding; the grid wraps automatically with no horizontal scrolling.
Audio-only is now an option inside the Media format picker instead of a separate switch; playlists no longer show a format row and always queue video.
Playlist and torrent pickers: entries are hug-sized cards that flow automatically — no fixed column count, sized to their text.
Playlist and torrent pickers: entries are now hug-sized cards in a grid — rounded, spaced, and sized to their text.
Media preview errors use the row layout again, with the error message as the subtitle and Retry as a suffix button.
Playlist and torrent pickers: grid columns adapt to the item count so no row is left with an empty slot, with HIG spacing between cells.
Playlist and torrent pickers: dropped the custom selection tick; selected items now use the native highlight only.
Playlist and torrent pickers now lay out in a grid (up to 4 columns), with a tick marking selected items.
HLS downloads: the progress grid follows sharp downward revisions of the size estimate instead of stalling on a phantom spike.
Fix a build failure in the probe-error card.
Probe errors render as plain text: messages containing markup-like characters (e.g. <HTTPError 403>) no longer fail to display.
Media-preview error state redesigned as a left-aligned, vertically centered card.
Playlist and torrent pickers use pure Adwaita defaults with no custom styling.
Playlist and torrent pickers redesigned: native single-column list with compact single-line rows.
Download progress bars now expose screen-reader labels.
URL lookup desensitizes the Add button instead of freezing the whole URL row.
Install popover padding corrected and generic file icon fixed.
Failure dialog shows the actual error instead of stale status text.
Download rows restored to 4.4.4 12px inner padding.
Inline New Download: removed the video title/URL header between the URL entry and options.
Menu-triggered New Download slides down smoothly (deferred past the menu close).
Inline New Download UI uses HIG AdwPreferencesGroup with native row padding; download entries use GtkListBox with .boxed-list-separate.
Window margins unified at 12px for the inline card and the download list.
New Download card: the Add (✓) button stays visible after the lookup, so a second press adds the download.
Playlist picker uses up to 4 columns in a most-square grid with no empty cells (3→3×1, 4→2×2, 8→4×2).
Media format and Audio only preview rows are single-line.
New Download URL row uses HIG AdwPreferencesGroup → AdwEntryRow with apply button as the Add action.
Playlist picker columns adapt by divisor so no cell is ever empty (3→3, 4→2×2).
New Download card uses HIG AdwPreferencesPage/Group/EntryRow with apply button for the URL field.
Playlist picker grid adapts columns to item count with no empty cells; selected entries get an accent outline.
The New Download card no longer stretches full-width; it is centered with proper spacing, and its URL field and buttons are vertically aligned.
Playlist and torrent pickers have proper spacing around their grids.
Byte sizes now use the system locale's formatting.
Restored brotli and deflate HTTP compression support.
The "of" in progress amounts ("900 MB of 2.0 GB") is now translatable.
The New Download card now toggles open and closed from the + button, Ctrl+N, or the empty-state button, and its header is one compact row: URL field, Add Download, options gear, and close.
The lookup indicator is now a spinner inside the URL field, with no layout shift while a link resolves.
Live recordings recover when the stream's formats change during setup: Grab re-resolves once and retries with fresh formats, and no longer claims a recording was kept when nothing was recorded.
Download rows now show a media-type icon (video, audio, playlist, torrent, or file), and the status filter is a segmented control that appears only when there are downloads to filter.
File name, torrent file, and save location moved behind a gear toggle that reveals them inline under the URL field.
Fixed a crash when adding a download, and empty .grab-video staging folders are now removed once their downloads finish.
Red is now reserved for failure: the live-capture icon is no longer red, while failed downloads and install errors tint their icons red.
The New Download dialog is now an inline card pinned under the header bar. It opens in place, so the download queue stays visible and usable while it is open.
Closing the card now fully resets it — media format picker, audio switch, and lookup state — so reopening it always starts fresh.

Live captures now stage their in-progress files in the hidden .grab-video folder next to the destination, like regular downloads. If a recording fails but the media is kept, the failure message now names the folder it was kept in.
Unified downloads now stage their in-progress files in a hidden .grab-video folder next to the destination instead of /tmp, so large downloads no longer fill up tmpfs.
Live captures with the from-start toggle on now fall back to recording from the live edge when the stream doesn't support from-start, instead of failing.
Merged MP4s now place the moov atom at the front, so playback can start before the whole file has arrived.
Fixed live captures aborting when extra downloader arguments were passed along with the URL.
The downloader capability probe no longer blocks background async work while it runs.
Collection folders no longer follow a pre-existing symlink with the same name; they use a fresh folder instead.
Live captures now pass timestamp-alignment flags to the downloader, keeping split audio and video tracks in sync without re-encoding.
Playlists and multi-item stories now download into a folder named after the collection.
Adding a download whose file already exists fails the row instead of renaming it; existing files are never overwritten.
Live downloads now fail clearly when the recorder errors, instead of keeping a partial capture.
Playlist rows now download the entry you picked instead of the playlist's first entry repeating.
yt-dlp now uses Chrome's TLS fingerprint where supported, fixing downloads that stalled or stopped early.
The quickjs download is now verified against pinned SHA-256 checksums with a size cap.
The Add dialog no longer starts a second lookup when you press Enter while a lookup for the same link is still running.
Fixed "No suitable formats found" for direct video files that don't declare an audio track, such as some Instagram stories.
Fixed the Add dialog getting stuck with no preview after editing a link back and forth; lookups no longer stay suppressed.
The tarball install prompt now installs quickjs-ng with a single distro command line alongside yt-dlp and ffmpeg.
The tarball install prompt now covers quickjs alongside yt-dlp and ffmpeg: no distro packages it, so its row installs Grab's pinned binary with one click instead of a terminal command.

Subtitles are now resolved with a best-effort probe before the download: the configured language when offered, otherwise English, otherwise none. yt-dlp embeds them directly on the media invocation, so a subtitle fetch failure can no longer sink the download.
Unknown-container downloads now adopt the tallest in-cap file instead of the first in extractor order, so Best no longer lands on a low resolution when a site lists direct files with no codec info.
The stall watchdog is now exempt during the merge phase, since yt-dlp captures ffmpeg's output and a successful merge is silent on both streams.
YouTube downloads using cookies now install QuickJS as yt-dlp's JS runtime on first use, restoring the full format list for authenticated player clients.
HLS downloads now rebuild the progress block grid whenever the reported total grows, so the grid no longer fills up while the download is still in progress.
Stalled video downloads are now detected and stopped instead of hanging until the whole-attempt timeout: a watchdog watches piece throughput and aborts downloads that stop making progress.
Importing a large playlist no longer refreshes the queue and persists it once per row — the UI updates once when the import finishes.
Every spinner in the app now uses AdwSpinner.

Fixes downloads landing on the lowest quality after picking a higher one: formats that carry a video height are no longer eligible as the audio track, so the HLS quality preset is reached instead of being suppressed by a misclassified direct file.
Restores the secrets permission in the Flatpak manifests: the yt-dlp subprocess needs Secret Service over D-Bus to decrypt Chromium-based browser cookies, and without it cookie probing failed.
The browser-access row no longer re-checks itself while visible — flatpak overrides only apply at sandbox startup, so Preferences now shows a hint to restart Grab after running the command instead.
The media-tool install rows swap their spinner and status icon through a stack, and the restart hint row is no longer activatable.
Fixes live recordings failing at finalize: the remux now tells ffmpeg the container format explicitly instead of letting it guess from the .part filename.

description.p: The Flatpak no longer bundles Deno or requests the secrets permission, and grants no browser-profile access by default. Preferences now shows the exact read-only flatpak override command for the selected browser when its profile is unreachable in the sandbox, re-checking while visible so the row dismisses itself once the override lands. Also adds a Flathub submission manifest variant.
The browser-cookie export now uses the same yt-dlp identity flags as every other download, including the YouTube player-client workaround. Also a source-comment cleanup with no behavior change.

All .torrent archive reads now go through a bounded reader so a malformed archive can't exhaust memory, and oversized yt-dlp probe output is drained past the limit so a stuck pipe can no longer hang the video worker. Also a whole-code readability pass with no behavior change.

Hotfix: restores the Flatpak bundle to releases. The release-time bundle check was rewritten to inspect the build's ostree repository instead of the bundle file itself, so this release ships both the tarball and the Flatpak bundle again.

Video filenames no longer carry the video id (Title [id].mp4 becomes Title.mp4); the id is stored in the file's comment metadata instead. Every download now embeds metadata tags, and the "Audio quality" preference is gone — audio-only downloads always use yt-dlp's default quality.

Removing a video that is still downloading is now safe: the worker is stopped first and its temporary files are cleaned up only after it has exited, so a new download can no longer collide with the cleanup. Interrupted live recordings are kept rather than deleted, and retries no longer destroy them.

Stopping a live recording now says so: the row button reads Stop Recording and confirms the recording is kept. The tools install progress uses a proper loading indicator that no longer freezes or misaligns.

Beta: video filenames no longer carry the video id (Title [id].mp4 becomes Title.mp4); the id is stored in the file's comment metadata instead. Every download now embeds metadata tags, and the "Audio quality" preference is gone — audio-only downloads always use yt-dlp's default quality.

Removing a video that is still downloading is now safe: the worker is stopped first and its temporary files are cleaned up only after it has exited, so a new download can no longer collide with the cleanup. Interrupted live recordings are kept rather than deleted, and retries no longer destroy them.
Also ships the id3 dependency update (a decoded-frame size limit that stops ID3 decompression bombs).
Internal restructuring of the video, download, and window code into focused modules; the HLS block map also restarts on a fresh grid when a later leg is much larger than the first.
Embedded subtitles no longer leave a sidecar file alongside the video, and Clear Finished greys out when nothing is finished.
Hotfix: the tools install popover no longer stalls on "Downloading" after the downloads complete — each row now flips to Installed with its probed version.
Beta: failed downloads can be retried from a toast with the failure count, the shortcuts dialog documents the queue search, and the internals get a cleanup pass.
Hotfix: the HLS block map rescales when totals refine upward instead of staying flood-lit on its first tiny estimate, and second legs start empty.
Non-video Drive links fall back to direct download, Add works on short and unlisted video links, yt-dlp fragments run serially, and the HLS block map no longer flashes on estimate wobble.
Beta: non-video Drive links fall back to direct download, Add works on short and unlisted video links that probe video-shaped, and yt-dlp fragment downloads return to the serial default.
Browser cookies now read the freshest Chromium channel profile, so daily-driven beta/nightly builds stop losing to a stale stable install.
Flatpak now ships the yt-dlp_linux build for keyring and impersonation support.
Fixes video extraction failures by excluding YouTube's web player client from every yt-dlp spawn, and bumps the gtk4 stack to the latest stable 0.11.5.
Direct-file probe bypass expanded to 149 extensions with dot-required terminals, so pasted files skip the wasted media probe while pages, feeds and streams stay probeable.

Single-invocation yt-dlp downloads with merge margin, original-language audio preference, playlist/story/highlight queue support with per-segment pages, live capture with edge fallback, remux-aware naming, HIG Preferences rewrite, batch intake routing, and offline-safe Flatpak vendor sync.

Audio-only download mode removed (preferences, per-download dialog override, and video-audio-only setting). Queue files with the removed audio_only key still parse. Simplified request plumbing and format-identity logic.

Machine-readable download progress, overwrite pre-flight for existing files, per-language subtitle sidecars for videos, finished-download history with clear and URL dedup, live recording indicator with part-shell cleanup, and part-name protection for foreign files.

Media downloads: quality picker with per-format sizes, live-stream capture with recording indicator, torrents follow SOCKS5 proxies. Indeterminate progress during resolving, dropped links open the media dialog, hardened staging and cookie handling.

Hotfix: video downloads work again (the tool check probed ffmpeg with the wrong flag and failed every attempt). Pausing or retrying a video now resumes its parts instead of restarting. Video tools setup reworked: tarball builds get guided terminal install instructions per distribution, and installations report staged progress in place.

Fix: video-page preview no longer stalls Add on canonicalized links, and metadata lookups time out with Retry instead of spinning forever. Video preferences show tool versions with install progress. More video sites supported. New Download dialog is now stepped: video details get their own page with thumbnail preview.
New: video-page downloads (YouTube, Vimeo and more) with quality picker up to 4K, audio-only mode, and automatic merging. The app is now licensed under GPL-3.0-only.
Test-reliability fix: the integration-test fixture server retries startup on fresh ports instead of flaking. No functional changes.
Code-health release: Undo restore state is passed as a single snapshot struct, and formatting/lint gates are clean. No functional changes from 2.4.3.
Code formatting cleanup (cargo fmt). No functional changes from 2.4.1.

Fix: FlatPark install instructions point at the correct repo file; Undo resumes segmented downloads instead of restarting them; queue restore validates before spawning engines; row UI tolerates widget drift without panicking. Security: CI workflows pin third-party actions to commit SHAs.

Fix: torrents set to seed with no stop rule stay active with live upload stats and a working Stop button, instead of showing Finished while still seeding in the background. The bulk-import batch guard is now a nesting-safe counter.
Security: torrent engines no longer overwrite files in collision-deduped output folders; a user-set User-Agent is sanitized to header-safe ASCII before use.

Fix: torrent output folders are deduplicated at intake so existing files are never overwritten; batch import skips comment lines; cancelling a torrent mid-add keeps partial files for resume; DHT toggle notes it applies after restart. Security: the download engine no longer follows HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect downgrades, and worker state recovers from lock poisoning instead of panicking.
Fix: a preset GSettings schema path that lacks this app's schema no longer aborts startup — it is ignored in favor of the app's own install tree.
Fix: the portable tarball no longer aborts on startup — the binary finds its GSettings schemas in its own install prefix, and the tarball ships compiled schemas.
Fix: the header search toggle is hidden when the queue is empty, and an open search bar collapses with the last entry.
New: GNOME HIG search pattern — a header-bar toggle reveals a search bar with the status filter alongside. Open it with the button, by typing, or with Ctrl+F.
Stability: removed per-download custom headers in favor of automatic headers. Internal code cleanups.

New: task search and status filter, multi-URL batch add, task rename. Torrent: upload stats on rows, custom trackers, seed ratio and time limits, listen port. Downloads: per-download custom headers, keep-server-file-date option, command-line URL enqueue.
Hardening: torrent archive handling is confined to the app data dir, duplicate settings key removed, peer-limit edge case fixed.
Fix: About dialog no longer crashes; release notes are embedded in the app.
Dialog improvements: access keys on action buttons, clearer file-chooser labels, About page with release notes, Enter key confirms dialogs. Dependency updates.
Fix: URL apply tick returns after failed validation so over-long URLs can be corrected and retried.
Full interface translation support (gettext); typed settings access throughout.
Fix: finished torrents are evicted from the session, stopping RAM growth; leaner per-tick updates; refreshed screenshots.
Refreshed AppData screenshots: block maps and the new preferences pages.
Per-block download map: click a downloading row to reveal downloaded blocks; HIG separator between progress bar and blocks.
Torrent delete moves the real download folder to Trash; magnets download into their own subfolder; file-picker leftovers are cleaned at finish; peer limit defaults to unlimited.
Fix: finished torrent downloads keep their .torrent file so deleting them moves the real download folder to Trash.
Fix: deleting a torrent download now moves the real download folder to Trash, and re-adding a torrent right after deleting it no longer fails with a phantom already-in-queue error.
Change: the torrent file picker no longer remembers past selections, opening a .torrent file shows the same file list as the picker, and downloading rows show how many files are selected.
New: the torrent file picker remembers your per-file selection, so re-adding the same torrent pre-checks your last choice.
Maintenance: regression coverage for per-file torrent selection. No user-facing changes.
Fix: re-adding an already-queued torrent with a different file selection now fails fast instead of silently adopting the wrong files. Grab no longer claims to be a web browser.
Fix: per-file torrent selection now survives app restarts instead of silently downloading everything.
Code cleanup: removed dead code and merged duplicate helpers. No behavior changes.

Torrent support: magnet links and .torrent files with a file picker, multi-file torrents in their own folder, a dedicated Torrent preferences page, and network settings on their own page. Removing a torrent keeps partial files so Undo resumes instead of restarting.
Security hardening: download folders must be absolute paths, URLs with embedded credentials are rejected, fresh downloads claim their destination atomically, and redirects are capped at five hops.
Main thread never blocks on portal or file I/O (async bus lookups, worker-thread list imports), and diagnostics move to structured tracing logs.
Fixes the suspend block never engaging (portal flags are positional), plus duplicate-request fencing and diagnostic logging.
Release bundles now build clean in CI and attach automatically; test bundles build on demand and on packaging pull requests. Distribution is Flatpak-only.
Adaptive piece sizing for huge files, stall hardening, cross-desktop sleep inhibit with toggle, background portal support, and Flatpak-only distribution.
Hardened downloads: verified sizes, resumable retries, healing server changes, per-row retry, and a full review pass over engine and interface.
Queue-for-later button, auto-park when lowering simultaneous downloads, no more phantom failures or flickering progress on re-queued rows.
Finished-download notifications show just the filename.
Cancelled downloads no longer raise the failure banner; Cancel All is a single pass with no stray background tasks.
Cancel All now asks for confirmation first; background notification simplified to a single line.
First stable release: segmented downloads with smart auto-resume, pause/resume, download history, live preferences, and a native HIG-compliant interface.
First beta: native HTTP backend with pause/resume, segmented downloads, download history, and HIG-compliant UI.
Security hardening: capped split sizes, failed engine tasks report instead of stalling, stricter filenames.
Progress rows show downloaded-of-total amounts; background notice only while transferring.
Download speed measures new bytes only, so resumed downloads read correctly.
Segmented downloads resume across restarts instead of starting over.
Survives killed segmented downloads without corrupting files; leaner engine and test helpers.
Survives throttling hosts by dropping to one stream; fixes segmented resume corrupting finished files.
Downloads take the server-advertised filename, so video links save with the right extension.
Finished downloads show their final size where the speed was.
URL length limit, CI checks on every push, and contributor documentation.
New Download keeps its pill shape but sizes to its text instead of stretching full-width.
Smaller New Download button; header add button only shows alongside the download list.
HIG compliance pass: failure banner, undo for removals, keyboard shortcuts, screen-reader labels, and release hardening.
Native HTTP backend with pause/resume, background downloads, and download history.
Initial release.
